title: Derivation coefficient addition on the dual-number diagonal
statement: Let $S$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme], $D=S[\varepsilon]$ its dual-number thickening [def-sc-dual-numbers], and $X\to S$ any scheme over $S$. Let $f:D\times_S D\to X$ be an $S$-morphism and $g:S\to X$ a morphism. Write $z:D\to D$ for projection to $S$ followed by the zero section. Suppose the reductions of $f\circ(\mathrm{id},\mathrm{id})$, $f\circ(\mathrm{id},z)$ and $f\circ(z,\mathrm{id})$ all equal $g$. The relative derivations given by their epsilon coefficients, transported to $g_*\mathcal O_S$, satisfy $d_{f\circ(\mathrm{id},\mathrm{id})}(a)=d_{f\circ(\mathrm{id},z)}(a)+d_{f\circ(z,\mathrm{id})}(a)$ on every open and every section $a$.

source.place: Lemma 33.16.2 proof, square-zero pushout addition; sectionwise arbitrary-base form and group unit-law application

proof.text: Compare the iterated thickening S[epsilon][delta] to D times_S D by its two projections. Product extensionality identifies its two axes with the categorical axes and its single-to-double diagonal with the categorical diagonal. The diagonal is constructed sectionwise by x mapping to x.fst + inr x.snd.fst; locality follows because units are detected by the constant coefficient.

The diagonal section map is identity on both dual-number inclusions. For a ring map q with those properties, q(inr(inl r))=inr r. Also inr(inr r)=inl(inr r)*inr(inl 1), so its image is zero. Expand x into its four coefficients and apply additivity: (q x).snd=x.fst.snd+x.snd.fst. The first summand is the first-axis coefficient and the second is the second-axis coefficient. Apply this to the comorphism of f on each open.

The equations of the three reductions identify their underlying maps with g, hence identify the inverse-image opens and the pushforward module structures. The definitions of infDerivation and equality transport turn the preceding coefficient equation into the asserted equation of relative derivation components. This includes the zero-ring and empty-base cases.
